 Oct 21, 2026 - Why Wipro Share Price is Rising 
 Why Wipro Share Price is Rising
 Oct 21, 2026 
 Image source: alexsl/www.istockphoto.com 
 The IT sector has become a key driver for India's economic growth, contributing significantly to the country's GDP and welfare.
 With digital tech advancing across industries, India stands at the forefront of the next big tech revolution. One name that stands out in this wave of growth is Wipro.
 Wipro is a leading global IT, consulting and business process services company headquartered in Bengaluru that operates globally across 65 countries.
 Today, the stock has surged up to 4%, making headlines across trading floors and financial platforms.
 Here's a closer look at the factors driving this impressive surge.
 # Sectoral Momentum
 Indian IT stocks saw strong buying on Wednesday, 21 October 2026, with Wipro shares rising up to 4% during the day, while the Nifty IT index jumped up to 2.6%.
 The main reason behind this rally is the positive mood in the IT sector. Better-than-expected Q2 results from IT companies have boosted investor confidence. Investors are also hopeful that business conditions are improving.
 The rally was broad-based, with all Nifty IT constituents trading in positive territory, indicating strong buying interest across the sector. Meanwhile, Accenture's guidance for the next financial year has renewed optimism around traditional IT spending, raising hopes that demand for technology services could improve.
 Overall, strong Q2 results, improving investor confidence, and hopes of higher IT spending are supporting Wipro shares and the broader IT sector.
 What's Next for Wipro? 
 Going forward, Wipro is making significant investments in AI, cloud, cybersecurity, consulting, and platform-led services, which can support long-term growth.
 To strengthen its position in an AI-first world, the company is pivoting to a services-as-a-software model through the AI Native Business & Platforms unit.
 The company seeks to deepen relationships with existing clients by expanding the range and complexity of services offered, aiming to drive higher wallet share and long-term growth.
 How Wipro Shares Have Performed Recently
 In the past five trading sessions, the stock has gained 8.5%, extending its one-month rally to 14.6%.
 However, over the past year, the shares are down 21.9%.
 The stock touched its 52-week high of Rs 273.15 on 22 December 2025 and its 52-week low of Rs 156.6 on 30 September 2026.
 About Wipro
 Wipro is a leading global IT, consulting and business process services company headquartered in Bengaluru, that operates globally across 65 countries.
 The company was incorporated in 1945 as Western India Vegetables Product. It was a consumer care product manufacturer till 1980 after which it diversified into the IT services business.
 With effect from 1 April 2012, the company demerged its other divisions (consumer care and lighting, medical equipment, and infrastructure engineering) into a separate company called Wipro Enterprises.
 Wipro's operations can be broadly classified into IT Services, IT Products, and India State Run Enterprise.
